newsitem.title: USA: SEC sues for insider Gillette-Duracell tip.
newsitem.headline: SEC sues for insider Gillette-Duracell tip.

text.p: People who were apparently tipped off before last week's announcement of a merger between Gillette Co. and Duracell International Inc. pocketed $1 million in illegal profits from the deal, the Securities and Exchange Commission charged Monday.

A lawsuit filed in Manhattan Federal Court alleged the unknown parties bought 1,700 call options on Duracell in the days before the Sept. 12 merger in accounts in Switzerland and the Bahamas that were designed to conceal their identities. A call option gives an investor the right to buy the stock at a set price.
Duracell's stock jumped about 27 percent, from $49.125 on Sept. 11 to $58.125 on Sept. 12 and $62.42 on Sept. 13, the lawsuit said. It said the parties sold their options for a profit of $950,000.
The options cost between 50 cents and $1.25. BSI-Banca de la Svizzera and Nominees (Bahamas) Ltd. declined to identify who set up the accounts, the suit said.
Gillette declined to comment on the lawsuit.
The suit seeks to enjoin the unknown parties from violating SEC regulations and force them to disgorge their illegal profits and pay fines.
Analysts say the $7 billion marriage between the razor giant and Duracell, the worldwide leader in alkaline batteries, should boost sales of both companies' products.
Gillette's stock fell 75 cents to $69.625, and Duracell slid $1.125 to $61.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
